question: What does the name Masjid al-Aqsa mean, and what are its other names?
answer:
So al-Aqsa means the furthest-most. Al-Aqsa means that which is the furthest. And Masjid al-Aqsa is called Masjid al-Aqsa because it was the furthest masjid from Mecca at the time frame when the religion of Islam, when the Qur'an, was revealed. The furthest place from Mecca that we can call a masjid, that Allah 'azza wa jall called to be a place of worship, is Masjid al-Aqsa. And it is the furthest masjid that is visited from Mecca and from Medina as well. Mecca and Medina are relatively closer together; Aqsa is the furthest from them.

And one can also say al-Aqsa could imply sanctity and holiness: it is the furthest removed from filth and from being sacrilege. So al-Aqsa means the exalted, one can also say. So these are the meanings of Masjid al-Aqsa.

Now, there are other names for Masjid al-Aqsa as well, and the Qur'an uses a number of these names, and the hadith also mentions these names. Of the names, one of the most common names, especially in the hadith, is Bayt al-Maqdis: the house that is sanctified. And house here means house of Allah, like we call the Ka'bah Bayt Allah, the house of Allah. So al-Aqsa has been called Bayt al-Maqdis: the house that is pure, the house that is sanctified, the house that is holy.

It is also called Bayt al-Muqaddas. It is spelt the same, Maqdis and Muqaddas, but there's a slight difference in meaning here. Muqaddas means that which is purified, that which has been made holy. So that is a masjid that has been made holy, sanctified, blessed. Anybody who prays there also becomes blessed. So this is another title, Bayt al-Muqaddas.

Of course, in ancient Hebrew it is called Yerushalam, and this means the city of peace. So we call it in Arabic Bayt as-Salam, the city of peace: Shalam or Shalom in Hebrew, and Salam in Arabic. So it is called the abode or the land of peace.

Now, when the Romans conquered Bayt al-Maqdis, when they conquered al-Aqsa, they wanted to destroy its Jewish heritage. And so they Latinized it; they gave it a Latin or a Roman name, and they called it Aelia Capitolina. This is the name that was given to it by the Romans, by the Byzantines. And when the Prophet ﷺ was preaching in Mecca, it was controlled by the Romans, by the Byzantine empire, and this was the name that it was called by. And for simplicity's sake, they would call it Iliya. And so in the hadith in Sahih Bukhari and other hadith, we find the name Iliya for Jerusalem. So this is a name that it was commonly known as because of the Byzantine Empire, because of the Roman Empire.

And Iliya, or Aelia Capitolina: Aelia goes back to the family name of the emperor Hadrian. The emperor's family is the Aelia family, and so they named it after the emperor. And Capitolina was something that was for one of their gods, I believe Jupiter or something.

After the collapse of the Byzantine empire, this name is completely gone. But if you read books of history, especially books that talk about this time frame, and even our own books (as we said, Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim and all of the books of hadith), you find Bayt al-Maqdis, Bayt al-Muqaddas, and you also find Iliya. And this is because it was known by that during the time of the Sahaba; during the time of the conquest, it was called Iliya. So these are all names that have been used. There are more than these, but these are the primary names.
